elements.name: TextBox 37
elements.text:
- 6G applications need simultaneous communication and high-precision sensing. Cell-free massive MIMO ISAC avoids duplicated spectrum, but imperfect CSI and non-convex resource allocation hinder deployment.
- Gap: a nearest/path-loss AP cluster can contain APs with zero dedicated sensing power, so nominal selection is not physically meaningful participation.
- Aim: minimise total transmit power while meeting robust communication SINR, sensing SINR and position-PCRB tracking constraints.
- Thesis claim: AP-target participation must be optimised jointly with robust beamforming to obtain physically feasible, energy-efficient sensing clusters.
- Evidence is reported only after fixed-topology re-optimisation and explicit feasibility validation.

elements.name: rationale_text
elements.text:
Cell-free ISAC must retain globally cooperative communication while using a sparse and physically meaningful sensing cluster. We minimize transmit power under robust communication SINR, sensing SINR, and PCRB tracking constraints.

The association b_mp gates only the target-p dedicated sensing waveform S_p. Communication covariances remain globally cooperative.
